provenance.note: A home upright for a cassette: a little out of tune, a clear hammer and a short fall, bright enough that a tape's lost top still leaves the notes; meant to be played through a worn tape head.

notes.copiedFrom: piano, its numbers changed for a soft keys backdrop; held at nought (AWAITING) until a part admits it
notes.timbres: none declared yet: the loudness fit measures a timbre when a part admits the row
notes.string: The deep house keys' string (round liquid-keys-2, his word 10-29 on the old grands the liquid keys draw: "yeah, that's the trick we might want to pull updated piano there as well"): the piano row's stiff string, wooden board and felt hammer in place of the six partials and the band of hiss, keeping this row's own envelope, lid (brightMin and brightMax), unison and high-pass, with the small box, a stiffer string for its 3-cent stretch, a short felt. Its `register` is its level by register against this row's six partials, measured note by note (MIDI 36-88, velocities 0.5 and 0.6, 3 s from the strike, dry): every register plays as loud as it did, the mean difference under 0.55 dB.
